shipped_rows.title_o: The cost of blocking the mirror generalization process in reading: evidence for the role of inhibitory control in discriminating letters with lateral mirror-image counterparts

blind_target.evidence_quote: A previous study demonstrated that preventing mirror errors in reading requires the inhibition of the mirror generalization process in expert adult readers (Borst et al., 2015). Using the same experimental paradigm, the current study aimed at replicating this result in school-aged children.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Crucially, children required more time to determine that two animals facing opposite directions were identical when preceded by two letters that were lateral mirror images of one another (b/d) than when preceded by letters that were not mirror images of one another (f/t). Importantly, the amplitude of the negative priming effect did not vary with age. Our results suggest that overcoming mirror errors in reading, regardless of the reading proficiency of school-aged children, is rooted in the ability to inhibit the mirror generalization process.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract states the original inhibitory mechanism and reports the corresponding negative priming result in the new sample. The proposed age effect is an extension rather than a contradicted original result.

luna_triage.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the Borst et al. (2015) empirical finding about inhibition of mirror generalization in expert adult readers and says it is being replicated. Shipped row 2136 is the Borst et al. paper on that same finding; the 2014 DOI year is consistent with a report appearing in 2015.
